Hi Lina — thanks for the clear checklist. Attaching a compact response pack to accelerate procurement. Highlights below and the attachments include: a filled SSQ, an annotated dataflow diagram (v1), and a DPA redline for your review.

High-level answers (short):
- Classification: Redwood does not re-classify customer data; we map incoming fields to PII categories you specified in the SSQ. By default we treat: names, emails, phone numbers, MRNs as "direct identifiers." Model inputs flagged as identifiers are eligible for tokenization/pseudonymization at ingest per customer config. See SSQ mapping page 2.

- Persistence & caches: Raw identifiers are not written to durable shared stores. Inference runtime uses ephemeral KV caches per-request/instance; we do not persist those caches to S3 or long-term DBs. Our default telemetry redaction strips direct identifiers from logs; customers can opt-in to additional telemetry.

- Pseudonymization & tokenization: We offer an ingest-time tokenization plugin (customer-managed KMS optional). With the plugin enabled, original identifiers are replaced with stable tokens before they hit the model. Token vaults can be hosted in the customer's VPC or in Redwood's KMS-backed service (we call this "Managed Token Vault").

- Subprocessors & transfers: Current subprocessors used for model hosting (GPUs), telemetry, and CI/CD are listed in the attached subprocessors appendix in the DPA. For HealthBridge's expected EU-region hosting request: we can either (1) host in an EU partner region (no cross-border transfer), or (2) if hosted in the US, we will rely on SCCs + appropriate technical controls. We flagged EU-hosting options in the dataflow diagram.

Marissa — quick technical clarifications to incorporate into the diagram and SSQ answers before we send the final pack: 

1) KMS custody options: we need to explicitly call out three KMS flows in the diagram and SSQ: 
   - Customer-managed KMS (VPC) for token vaults (no Redwood access)
   - Customer KMS + Redwood-managed proxy (Redwood has blind-encrypt access only; no plaintext in our control plane)
   - Redwood-managed KMS (operational mode) for customers that choose us to host keys (we should specify HSM-backed option and key rotation cadence).

2) Telemetry & logs: add a note that inference traces may include token hashes only; raw token values are redacted. Retention default 30 days for operational logs; 90 days for aggregated telemetry. Offerability: HealthBridge can request shorter retention in contract.

3) Subprocessor EU-hosted vs US-hosted branch: the diagram should show two parallel paths — EU-hosted (no export) and US-hosted (SCCs + encryption in transit + geo-fencing). That will answer procurement's transfer concern.

4) Model cache lifetime: explicitly state default KV lifetime (60s) and that cache eviction occurs on instance restarts; no write-to-disk.

If you want, I can mark up redwood-dataflow-diagram_v1.png with these callouts; also suggest changing filename to _v2.

—Karthik
